messages.author: dba8d1ebc846c330
messages.subject: plotting time series
parts:
Dear Rkoholiki,

I am working at the moment with three time series of temperature. Now I
wanted to use ts.plot(), because with this function you can plot more
time series in one plot. Now I tried it but it does not work. You get
the following warning "Error in .cbind.ts(list(...), .makeNamesTs(...),
dframe = dframe, union = TRUE) : no time series supplied".

Here is an example (copy and paste into R):

maxtemp <- c(20,24,25,29,21,25)
meantemp <- c(19,22,22,26,19,22)
mintemp <- c(16,19,28,22,15,18)
cbind(maxtemp,meantemp,mintemp)

ts.plot(maxtemp,meantemp,mintemp,lty=c(1:3))

Apparently it does not read my time series. Can someone help with this
problem?

Hvala!

Maarten

messages.author: 08f3062efe0fd1ca
messages.subject: Re: [Rkoholiki] plotting time series
parts:
The problem is that ts.plot demands a ts class object. Your mean, max and mintemp objects are all vectors. As soon as I find the time, I will see how can POSIX elements be transformed into ts class.

See ?as.ts or ?is.ts and http://www.stat.pitt.edu/stoffer/tsa2/R_time_series_quick_fix.htm

Cheers,
Roman

messages.subject: Re: [Rkoholiki] plotting time series
parts:
Something like this? The plot is in need of tweaking, but I hope the general idea is clear. This was done in ggplot2 and the code to do all the steps is below.

setwd("/spajza1/r/help/maarten/")
library(ggplot2)

t.data <- read.table("lowertemp.txt", header=T, sep="")
t.data <- transform(t.data, date = paste(month, day, sep="-"))[,-c(1:2)] #melt day and month
date <- strptime(as.character(t.data$date), format="%B-%d") #convert date to POSIXct class
t.data <- cbind (t.data[, c(1:3)], date)

dta <- ggplot(t.data, aes(x=date, y=meantemp)) +
    geom_line(linetype="solid") +
    geom_line(aes(y=maxtemp), linetype="dashed") +
    geom_line(aes(y=mintemp), linetype="dotted")

jpeg(filename="marteenqtplot.jpg", width=800, height=600, units="px")
dta
dev.off()

messages.author: dba8d1ebc846c330
messages.subject: Re: [Rkoholiki] plotting time series
parts:
Thanks Roman!

I also found a way how to do it for ts.plot().

mintemp <- c(16,19,18,22,15,18)
ts.plot(ts(maxtemp),ts(meantemp), ts(mintemp), col=1:2,
main="ts.plot(maxtemp, meantemp, mintemp)", ylab="Temperature")

The catch is that you should put "ts" (time series) in front of the vector.

lp,

Maarten
